assessment:
The table sees Goblin Matron enter and waits for you to go and get a lord. Let them wait. Then name the removal, or the mana, or the enchantment — Matron searches for a Goblin CARD, and Gempalm Incinerator and Boggart Shenanigans both wear the word.

Know the split cold, because it decides which card you name. Matron delivers to your hand, so the fetch still has to be cast — kicker still gets paid, cycling still works, and a counterspell still gets its window. Moggcatcher puts a Goblin permanent straight onto the battlefield: no cast, nothing to counter, no kicker. Send finishers to hand, send engines to the battlefield.

Neither wish needs your commander, and that is the point. One of your three goldfish targets is gated on Zada; of five passing stacks only 001 and 003 put her on the board. So fetch for the swarm half and keep playing when she is answered — a wish spent insuring the commander is a wish spent on the smaller half of your deck.

Aim the wish at the group it can actually thicken. Your early-token component assembles in 60.0% of runs at mean turn 3.18, and three of its five cards are Goblins — so a turn-three Matron is a genuine extra copy of that component. The storm half is not reachable: at 26.5% of runs, 16.9% by turn six, it is built entirely out of sorceries, and no Goblin tutor has ever named one.

Time Moggcatcher like a land, not a spell. Four mana to cast and three more to use is seven, and your mean available mana does not reach seven until turn ten — so deploy him a full rotation before you want the wish, on a turn nobody is watching you, and spend the activation on an end step.

targets.scenario: The default. Turn 3, three lands, two Goblins on the battlefield, no ritual in hand and Zada still in the command zone. Nobody at the table is pointing anything at you yet.
targets.why: Buy the discount before you buy the payoff. Warchief makes every Goblin spell cost {1} less and hands the whole swarm haste, and at 4.59 mean available mana on turn five that {1} is a whole extra spell per turn — which is the only thing a storm count ever cared about. Stack 004 shows the discount doing its job: under Warchief, Krenko costs {1}{R}{R} and taps the turn he arrives. Name Warchief, cast him next turn, and let the discount pay back the tempo Matron cost you.

citations.quote: tutoring is fewer slots but costs board impact and a turn of tempo

targets.scenario: Behind. The board just got swept, you are rebuilding on four lands, and the control player to your left has four mana open again — assume a second sweeper.
targets.why: Rebuild with the cheap card, not the best one. Marshal is three bodies on one card — a token when he enters, another when he dies — and the goldfish only walks you back to 4.07 bodies by turn five, so he beats your whole rebuild curve on his own. Let the echo lapse when you want that second token immediately; pay it when the body is doing real blocking. Do not name your most expensive Goblin into an open sweeper.

citations.quote: k tutors plus the card act like k+1 copies of *every* card

targets.scenario: Closing. Five bodies on the battlefield, an opponent at 11, one or two blockers in the way, and two mana up after Matron resolves.
targets.why: Name him and pay the kicker: creatures you control get +1/+0 and gain haste the moment he enters. This is the wish only Matron can grant, because kicker is paid as you cast the spell — put him onto the battlefield instead and you get an unkicked 1/1 and nothing else. On the 5.26 bodies the goldfish has you holding at turn six, that is six extra points arriving with haste. Count the damage before you fetch, not after.

targets.scenario: The one nobody sees coming. An opposing lord or a fat blocker is holding your entire swarm hostage, your hand is all gas, and you have drawn no answers.
targets.why: Pull removal out of a creature tutor. Cycle him for {1}{R} to deal damage equal to the number of Goblins on the battlefield — count their Goblins too, they add to your total — and draw a card on the way. Cycling only works from your hand, so route this wish through Matron every single time. Your interaction covers two permanent classes against a five-class target, so treat every answer you can manufacture as one you cannot replace.

tutors.notes: Once the errand is run she is just a Goblin body — count her for Krenko, tap her for Brightstone Ritual, feed her to Skirk Prospector. She finds Goblin cards, not Goblin creatures, so Boggart Shenanigans is a legal name on a grinding table. One card to skip while Zada sits in the command zone: Siege-Gang Lieutenant only makes its tokens if you control your commander, and you do not.

targets.scenario: The default. Turn 6 or 7, Moggcatcher untapped from last turn, three mana spare at the end step before your turn, a couple of Goblins out and Impact Tremors or General Kreat already on the battlefield.
targets.why: Skip the cast and give the table nothing to answer: there is no spell here, only the ability. Four bodies land at once — the Commander plus three tokens — and stack 002 already settled the arithmetic that every body entering is a point at every seat, so with Impact Tremors down that is 4 to each opponent before your turn even begins. Then each spare Goblin converts at {1}{R} into 2 damage pointed anywhere. Do it on the end step, never on your own main phase.

targets.scenario: Behind. A tax effect has turned your two-spell turns into one-spell turns, or an artifact deck is running away on Treasures.
targets.why: Go and get the repeatable out rather than a one-shot, and go and get it at instant speed — this is an activated ability, so the wish happens on their end step. Trashmaster sacrifices a Goblin to destroy target artifact, again and again, and you manufacture Goblins for a living. Break the first lock piece cheaply; it is the second and third that actually end you. Your answers cover two permanent classes against a five-class target, so buy the one that keeps answering.

targets.scenario: Closing. A haste lord already down — Warchief, Chieftain or Howlsquad Heavy — four Goblins on the battlefield, an opponent at 20 with no untapped blockers, and three mana in your main phase.
targets.why: Put him onto the battlefield with no cast and no counter window, and let the lord give him haste so he taps immediately. Stack 004 counts the swing on exactly this board: five Goblins become ten, 13 hasted power. Take the burst and build the whole turn around one activation — stack 004 is explicit that a Krenko fed to Skirk Prospector stays in the graveyard, because Zada is your commander and he is not. Without a haste lord down, fetch something else and take Krenko when the lord arrives.

citations.quote: Know your deck's tells — the cards everyone fears — and time them for the turn they win, not the turn they impress.

targets.scenario: The one nobody sees coming. A grinding table where your tokens die in bulk every rotation, and Blasphemous Act is sitting in your hand.
targets.why: Use a creature tutor to put an enchantment onto the battlefield. Shenanigans is a Kindred Enchantment — Goblin, so it is a Goblin permanent card and a perfectly legal wish, and nobody at the table plays around it. Afterwards every Goblin funeral is a point of damage you may point at a player. Fetch it before you cast Blasphemous Act, never after, and turn your own reset into a burn spell.

tutors.notes: He taps to do it, so he does nothing the turn he lands — deploy him a rotation early, on a quiet turn, and hold the activation. He is a Human Mercenary, so neither tutor can find him, Krenko does not count him and Prospector cannot eat him. And never plan to cast and activate him in one turn: that is seven mana, and your curve does not get there until turn ten.

gaps:
Both wishes are Goblin-shaped, so the entire spell half of this list is unreachable. Nothing here finds a ritual, a storm payoff, Impact Tremors, Skullclamp or Frontline Heroism — your second copy hub is a plain enchantment, so it arrives when you draw it and not a turn sooner. Stack 005's loop is the sharpest example: Haze of Rage is a sorcery and Storm-Kiln Artist is a Dwarf Shaman, so the best line in the deck can never be wished for.

Stop waiting on a tutor to assemble the big turn. Storm payoff plus ritual shows up in 26.5% of games, 16.9% of them by turn six, at mean turn 4.91 — and neither of these cards moves that number by a single point. Assemble it through draw instead: Faithless Looting, Idol of Oblivion, War Room, and the copied cantrips stack 001 verified.

What the wishes do reach is the token component — 60.0% of runs at mean turn 3.18, and three of its five cards are Goblins. So spend them on the board the copies need, and spend them on a turn where the payoff is already in your hand.
